note: Illustrative example for reviewing the format in B2. The guest is fictional. The capabilityCatalog below is a summary: the first six ids (email.drafts, email.send, calendar.book, crm.read, accounting.read, ledger.touch) now have real draft entries in docs/capabilities/ that await human review, while crm.write and accounting.paylinks stay unvetted on purpose, so the blocked design stays blocked. The real builder may only use vetted entries, and a design that needs an unvetted capability is flagged as no good fit.

evidence.fact: Spends about ten hours a week chasing quotes and unpaid invoices.
evidence.quote: It's about ten hours a week, easy, just chasing people.

evidence.fact: Technicians send quotes from the field-service app. Customers often go quiet afterwards.
evidence.quote: The guys send the quote from the app and then nothing. Silence.

evidence.fact: Around thirty quotes are open at any time.
evidence.quote: Thirty-ish open quotes at any given time.

evidence.fact: Does not check email during jobs. Replies late in the evening.
evidence.quote: I'm under a furnace all day. I do email at ten at night.

evidence.fact: Uses Gmail, a field-service app (Jobber) and QuickBooks Online.
evidence.quote: Everything is Jobber, Gmail and QuickBooks.

evidence.fact: Does not want follow-ups to feel like debt collection.
evidence.quote: I don't want to sound like a collections agency.

evidence.fact: A part-time office manager could approve routine messages.
evidence.quote: Priya's in two days a week and handles the books.

valueAssessment.problem: Owner chases open quotes and overdue invoices by hand.
valueAssessment.rule: estimated hours lost multiplied by confidence in the facts behind them
valueAssessment.confidence: high for the hours (read back and confirmed); medium for how much of that time can be automated
valueAssessment.dollarEstimateReason: The owner's hourly value and the quote conversion rate were not stated, so no dollar or revenue figure is claimed.

designs.name: Follow-up drafter

role.title: Follow-up assistant
role.objective: Prepare every quote follow-up and overdue-invoice reminder as a ready draft in Dana's own voice, so she only has to read and send.

model.why: Writing short, warm, plain messages is the whole job (e1, e6). About sixty drafts a week is light usage. Cost per week still to be measured.

skills.name: follow-up-writing
skills.why: Captures Dana's tone: warm, plain, no pressure (e6).

skills.name: quote-triage
skills.why: Decides which open quotes and invoices need a touch today, using the touch ledger.

tools.why: Remembers what was drafted for each quote and invoice, because each run starts fresh.

files: AGENTS.md: business rules, tone guide, who to escalate to

state.records: touch ledger (SQLite) kept on the employee's machine

notes.what: Short per-customer notes holding only facts Dana confirmed.
notes.editedBy: humans; the employee may propose additions in the digest but does not write them

routines.name: morning-drafts
routines.prompt: Find open quotes and overdue invoices that need a touch today. Create one Gmail draft for each, in Dana's voice. Record each in the ledger.
routines.approvals: none needed: it only creates drafts

routines.name: evening-digest
routines.prompt: Summarize the drafts waiting for review, oldest first, with one line on why each was chosen.

needsApproval: Every message: Dana or Priya reads and sends it
enforcedInCode: Only drafts can be created: the email.drafts capability has no send access.

expectedOutcome.metric: owner hours per week on follow-ups and reminders
assumptions: About 60 follow-ups and reminders a week (assumed from about 30 open quotes, e3, plus overdue invoices).
Writing each takes 5 to 8 minutes today; reviewing a ready draft takes 1 to 2 minutes (assumed).
The rest of the ten hours is phone calls and decisions, which stay with Dana.
Dana approves in the evening (e4), so some follow-ups go out a day later than they would otherwise.

accessNeeded.note: Credentials held on the host, never in this file.

risks: Follow-ups can still slip if drafts sit unreviewed (e4).

dataRetention.default: Delete message bodies after 90 days; keep the ledger.

pauseSwitch.how: Disable the employee's systemd timers with one command.
pauseSwitch.who: the operator, on the owner's request

approvalChannel.how: The evening digest links to each draft in Gmail; Dana or Priya reads and sends it.
approvalChannel.fallback: If nobody approves within two days, the digest flags the item as stale.

costEstimate.basis: Measure model usage plus a share of hosting over one trial week of routine runs, then project a month.

acceptanceChecks: After a morning run, every follow-up exists as a Gmail draft and nothing has been sent.
A quote with two ledger touches does not get a new draft without a flag.
The digest lists waiting drafts oldest first.

designs.name: Follow-up coordinator
designs.scope: Sends routine follow-ups and reminders within fixed rules. Drafts everything else.

role.title: Follow-up coordinator
role.objective: Keep every open quote and overdue invoice moving without Dana: send routine follow-ups on time, in her voice, and bring only the exceptions to her.

model.why: Same drafting job as d1, plus judgment on whether a case is routine or an exception (e6).

skills.name: follow-up-writing
skills.why: Dana's tone: warm, plain, no pressure (e6).

skills.name: quote-triage
skills.why: Chooses who needs a touch and checks the two-touch limit.

skills.name: escalation-rules
skills.why: Sends complaints, disputes, discounts and third touches to Dana, not to the customer.

tools.why: Needs to see whether a customer has already replied before sending (e5).
Enforces the two-touch limit and quiet hours across runs.

routines.name: quote-followups
routines.prompt: For open quotes with no reply after 3 days (first touch) or 7 days (second touch), send the follow-up if the case is routine. Draft anything outside the rules for Dana. Record every touch.
routines.approvals: routine cases send; exceptions become drafts

routines.name: invoice-reminders
routines.prompt: For invoices 7 days overdue (first reminder) or 14 days overdue (second reminder) and under the owner's limit, send the reminder. Draft everything else. Never send a third touch.
routines.approvals: routine cases send; exceptions become drafts

routines.name: evening-digest
routines.prompt: Summarize what was sent today, what replies came in, and the short list of items that need Dana's decision.

routines.name: weekly-report
routines.prompt: Report touches sent, replies, quotes won or lost where visible, and how many items were escalated, so the rules can be tuned.

alone: Send quote follow-up 1 (after 3 days) and 2 (after 7 days) in business hours
Send invoice reminder 1 (7 days overdue) and 2 (14 days overdue) for amounts under the owner's limit
Record every touch in the ledger
needsApproval: Any message that mentions a discount or a payment plan
Any customer who has replied with a complaint or a dispute
Any invoice over the owner's limit (limit to be set by Dana)
enforcedInCode: At most two automatic touches per quote and per invoice.
Sends only Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00 America/Toronto.
Never sends to a customer marked do-not-contact-automatically.
An invoice over the owner's limit becomes a draft, not a send.

About 70 percent of them are routine and fit the rules (assumed; measure in the first month).
Each exception takes Dana about 2 minutes.
The rest of the ten hours is phone calls and decisions, which stay with Dana.

recommendation.madeBy: system, after reading all three designs
reasons: It targets the confirmed problem of about ten hours a week chasing quotes and invoices (e1).
Dana only reads email late in the evening (e4). In d1 every message waits for her approval, so follow-ups slip a day. In d2 routine follow-ups go out on time.
The two-touch cap, business hours and escalation rules answer 'I don't want to sound like a collections agency' (e6).
d3 is blocked by two missing connectors and puts reply handling in Dana's name, which is more risk than the evidence supports for a first design.
caveats: Needs Dana's invoice limit and a choice of sending address.
The 70 percent routine share is an assumption to measure in the first month.

scheduleFormat: Schedules are systemd OnCalendar expressions, with the time zone kept in timeZone. Check each with systemd-analyze calendar on the server (not yet run).
